title: MRR, MAP, Recall@K & NDCG
interviewAnswer: Retrieval metrics depend on whether you care about finding any relevant result, all relevant results, or graded relevance near the top. MRR emphasizes first relevant rank; NDCG rewards graded relevance with position discount.
why: MRR, MAP, Recall@K & NDCG appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Retrieval metrics depend on whether you care about finding any relevant result, all relevant results, or graded relevance near the top. MRR emphasizes first relevant rank; NDCG rewards graded relevance with position discount. Recall@K matters for candidate stages. NDCG supports graded relevance. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: For support search, first-answer usefulness may make MRR important; for RAG candidate retrieval, Recall@K may dominate.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
